title: Design- Lead change messages, Assignment undone, 2.6 s close (design's version)
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} and {Technician-B} are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on.
    For example: ZZAUTOTEST C682430 Ana and ZZAUTOTEST C682430 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has three Approved work orders led by {Technician-A}: {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2} with {Technician-B} on one of its lines, and {Work-order-3}. None has a shift on the Schedule.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682430 Design Messages.
  • You have a stopwatch, for example on your phone.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Drag the card for {Work-order-1} onto the "Unassigned" column and let go.
  2. Drag the card for {Work-order-2} onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  3. Drag the card for {Work-order-3} onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  4. Click "Undo" on the message.
  5. Drag the card for {Work-order-3} onto {Technician-B}'s column again, let go and start the stopwatch.
  6. Keep the pointer away from the message and watch it.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the message reads "{Work-order-1} moved to Unassigned".
  • Step 2: the message reads "{Work-order-2} lead technician set to {Technician-B}".
  • Step 3: the message reads "{Work-order-3} assigned to {Technician-B}", with "Undo".
  • Step 4: {Work-order-3} goes back to {Technician-A}'s column and a new message reads "Assignment undone".
  • Step 5: the message shows, with a thin bar along its bottom.
  • Step 6: the bar runs out and the message closes about 3 seconds after you let go.

This case checks the DESIGN's version, which differs from the PRD: Message after moving a work order to Unassigned: the design shows "S1-352 moved to Unassigned"; the PRD says "{work order number} unassigned". Message when the new lead was already on the work order's crew: the design shows "S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards"; the PRD says always "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}". Message after clicking Undo: the design shows a new message "Assignment undone"; the PRD says "shows … no new toast". How long the lead-change message stays: the design shows about 2.6 seconds (a progress bar runs out in 2600 ms); the PRD says 8 seconds, held while the pointer is over it. It is held until Chris Ward rules on rows D02, D03, D04, D05 of the WO Board design-differences question sheet for Chris Ward (19 Oct 2026). Do not run it while it is held. If he rules for the design, it is released; if he rules for the PRD, it is removed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

What the PRD says instead:

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 66 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 19 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043

  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) reading “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”, or “{work order number} unassigned” after removing the lead, with an Undo button. Example: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”. This replaces the standard success toast for these two messages only.”
  • S4-R16: “The lead-change toast closes on its own after 8 seconds, stays open while the pointer is over it, and closes when Undo is clicked. Other success toasts dismiss automatically, as today.”
  • S4-R32: “Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was before the change: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician’s order, and any shifts the change cleared (removed shifts come back as they were; a shift that was ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back). Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry (S4-R9), follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (S4-N2), and shows no shift-clearing prompt and no new toast. If Undo cannot be saved, nothing changes and the alert “Couldn’t undo the change. Please try again.” shows.”

Not yet checked against a build.

References from Design

Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026 (Work Orders.dc.html and its flows, driven 14 Oct 2026), read 19 Oct 2026: the source of this case's expected results.

  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, toast wording: “label: !t ? srcId + " moved to Unassigned" : (wasCrew ? srcId + " lead technician set to " + t.name : srcId + " assigned to " + t.name)”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, after Undo: “toast: { label: "Assignment undone", tone: "info" }”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, toast timer: “animation: svToastBar 2600ms linear forwards;”
